clarifications: For a REAL event (estate sale, auction, geographic event, notable lot): strong seller-uploaded/event photography — cover image, site photographs, catalogue/lot photography, approved walkthrough-video frames — outranks generated merchandise. The Director decides whether authentic media is strong enough to anchor (readiness ≥ 70); if yes, no generated merchandise appears.
Catalogue/lot photography is added explicitly to tier 3/5 sources: a single strong lot photograph may anchor a notable-lot creative (tier 5 with one object) or supplement an environmental photograph.

Generated/representative merchandise and constructed scenes remain appropriate ONLY for generic buyer acquisition, generic seller acquisition, conceptual brand campaigns and any class where no real event/item is represented. Every such asset carries representative_not_lots and the render carries the disclosure line.

Generated representative merchandise must never masquerade as inventory: no lot numbers, no 'featured', no event facts beside representative objects; the judge asks 'does this look like it is showing real items from a specific sale?' — yes for a generic creative → fail.
Geographic event: WHAT / WHERE / WHEN / WHY LOOK; a real event uses its own photographs; landmark imagery (REF-22) is for generic geographic promotion only.
